title: bug: the stale-block #governors alert prunes a still-BLOCKED row's memo key whenever the row misses one sweep's alert condition, so the same block instance is paged again once a moving prerequisite stalls or the 2x bound passes, against its "a standing block alerts once" contract
description:
Filed by defect hunt #16 (task-151a2c54, architect-2a219562) on 2026-11-04. Found by the lane-2 subagent; the holder re-ran the repro and re-read the code at b9205914.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts:296-300 keys the memo of posted alerts by `taskId:blockedAt`, "so a re-block (new blockedAt) alerts again while a standing block alerts once". docs/MCP_SERVER.md `### moe.report_blocked`, Stale-block visibility (:1237), promises "once per block instance".
- The sweep adds a row's key to liveKeys (:410) only when the row qualifies this pass. A dependency-waiting row skips that line through `continue` in two cases: every prerequisite is met (:378), or its prerequisites are still moving and it is under 2x blockedTimeoutMs (:405). The prune at :419-423 then deletes the key, although the row is still BLOCKED under the same blockedAt. The prune's own comment says it drops only "blocks that resolved (or re-blocked under a new blockedAt)".
- Result: a row paged because its prerequisite was BLOCKED or BACKLOG is paged again for the same blockedAt. This happens once that prerequisite starts moving and then stalls again, or once the row passes the 2x bound.
- Restart: the memo is process memory (a WeakMap), so a daemon restart also re-pages every standing stale block once. Hunt #11 judged restart re-pages deliberate by analogy with recordCommit.ts:43-44. This module states no such policy, though, and its docblock and the contract both say once. The row must settle it either way (DoD 2).

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-151a2c54/B/zzHuntB_staleBlockOnce.test.ts, with its .output.txt beside it. In a git archive of b9205914, run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/zzHuntB_staleBlockOnce.test.ts`. It gives 2 failures:
  - case 2, one daemon lifetime: after the first alert at 90m, a second alert arrives for the same blockedAt, "⚠️ task-c0n5um (Test Task) has been BLOCKED 150m waiting on task-p4e4e…";
  - case 1, a fresh StateManager on the same .moe/: it re-alerts at 120m.
- Production (#governors, .moe/messages/chan-15c8e232.jsonl):
  - task-48f0b3aa was paged 8 times for one blockedAt, from 2026-10-31T08:27Z to 11-02T19:18Z;
  - task-1a8f1d0e was paged 7 times, the last at 2026-11-04T05:28:45Z.

FIX DIRECTION
- Within one lifetime: add the key to liveKeys for every resource-less BLOCKED row with a parseable blockedAt, before the qualification checks. The prune then drops only resolved or re-blocked rows.
- Restart: decide in the plan, with a test either way.
  - Option 1: persist the alerted keys in daemon-owned runtime state without touching packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts (held by task-77e54ebb).
  - Option 2: state, in the module docblock and the Stale-block visibility bullet, that a daemon restart re-alerts each standing block once, as recordCommit.ts:43-44 does for its window.
- Hunk ownership in docs/MCP_SERVER.md: edit only the Stale-block visibility bullet (:1237). The Ping routing bullets (:1241-1242) belong to task-31a2aa2f, filed in the same hunt. Distinct hunks merge cleanly in worktree mode, so no dependsOn.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md (### moe.report_blocked, Stale-block visibility only)
Nothing here is held by an open row at 06:01Z.
definitionOfDone: Within one daemon lifetime, a BLOCKED row is alerted at most once per blockedAt, even when it stops qualifying for a sweep and qualifies again later (the hunt repro's case 2, as a vitest case). A re-block under a new blockedAt, and a resolved-then-reblocked row, still alert again.

The restart behavior is decided and pinned by a test. Either a fresh StateManager on the same .moe/ does not re-alert a standing block (the repro's case 1), or the module docblock and the MCP_SERVER.md Stale-block visibility bullet say that a restart re-alerts each standing block once.
The existing dependencyUnblock tests pass. Any test that encoded prune-on-miss is named in the completion summary, together with why it changed.

(b) DoD 1's 'still alert again' half: 'pages a new block instance: a re-block under a new blockedAt, and a row resolved then blocked again'.

(c) DoD 2, the hunt repro's case 1 with a real post: 'a daemon restart reads #governors back: no second page for a standing block, a page for one it never paged'.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix both halves in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts (reference: prototype.diff).
1. Within one daemon lifetime:
- Add `function staleBlockKey(task: Pick<Task, 'id' | 'blockedAt'>): string`, returning `${task.id}:${task.blockedAt}`.
- In alertStaleBlocks's loop, right after `if (Number.isNaN(blockedAtMs)) continue;`: compute the key, call liveKeys.add(key), then `if (task.blockedResourceId || memo.has(key)) continue;`. The resource skip moves below the blockedAt parse. Delete the old key / liveKeys.add / memo.has block before the post.
- Every BLOCKED row with a parseable blockedAt is now live, resource-parked rows included. That is a superset of the row's FIX DIRECTION, so a row that goes resource-parked and back under one blockedAt is not re-paged either. The prune then drops only rows that left BLOCKED or changed blockedAt, as its comment already claims.
2. Restart. Decision: persist, by reading back the log the daemon already keeps.
- Add `function seedAlertedStaleBlocks(state: StateManager): Set<string>`. In alertStaleBlocks, create the memo with `memo = seedAlertedStaleBlocks(state)` instead of `new Set<string>()`.
- It finds the role channel named 'governors' in state.channels; with none it returns an empty set.
- It reads readTailJsonl(state, path.join(state.moePath, 'messages', `${channel.id}.jsonl`), CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES). Import both from './chatStore.js', add `import path from 'path'`, and add ChatMessage to the '../types/schema.js' type import.
- Error handling: ENOENT returns empty silently. Any other read error does one logger.warn and returns empty. It never throws: the worst case is one repeat page, never silence.
- For each line that includes ' has been BLOCKED ', JSON.parse it in try/catch. Keep only sender === 'system', with string content matching /^⚠️ (\S+) \(.*?\) has been BLOCKED /su and a parseable timestamp. Record the latest page time per task id. Copy the ⚠️ from an existing alert literal: it is U+26A0 U+FE0F.
- Then, for each BLOCKED row with a blockedAt whose latest page is strictly after Date.parse(blockedAt), add staleBlockKey(row). Strictly after, because every page of an earlier instance comes before that instance's resolution, and so before the next instance's blockedAt.
3. Comments:
- The memo docblock says what a block instance is, and that a fresh daemon seeds from #governors.
- In alertStaleBlocks's docblock, 'one line in #governors per block instance' gains 'a restart included'.
- seedAlertedStaleBlocks's docblock says it reads the newest CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES, the window chat_read serves. A page that has left that window (shown to no reader), or that never landed, is paged once more after a restart.
Then the three cases pass: 62 passed.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The stale-block #governors page fires at most once per block instance (taskId + blockedAt). Within one daemon lifetime, a row that stays BLOCKED under one blockedAt is never paged twice, however often it stops and starts qualifying. A fresh daemon seeds its memo from the newest CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES of #governors (the daemon's own sender 'system' pages, strictly after the row's blockedAt), so a restart does not re-page a standing block whose page is still in that window. A new instance (a new blockedAt, or BLOCKED again after a pass saw it leave) is paged again.
acceptanceCriteria: (a) A dep-waiting row paged at 1.5h on a BACKLOG prerequisite has exactly one page for its blockedAt, after the prerequisite moves (under 2x), the row passes 2x, and the prerequisite stalls again.
(b) A re-block under a new blockedAt gets a second page, and so does a row that a pass saw resolved and that is then blocked again.

(c) After a real page lands in #governors, a fresh StateManager on the same .moe/ does not page that standing block again. It does page a stale row the daemon never paged (a governor quoting the page format does not count) and a row re-blocked after its page.
The 59 existing dependencyUnblock tests pass unchanged, and the full daemon suite is green.
invariants: alertStaleBlocks never throws and never parks a row
A page is posted only for a qualifying row whose key is not in the memo
compatibility: No change to schema.ts, any MCP tool contract or any .moe/ path. The alert text and its four classes are unchanged.
Existing .moe/ state loads unchanged. The seed only reads #governors. An empty, missing or unreadable channel seeds nothing, which is the old behavior: one page per daemon lifetime.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Restart decided: persist (option 1), by reading back the #governors log the daemon already writes.
- Option 2 rejected: it documents a once-per-restart re-page, as recordCommit.ts:43-45 does, but the production evidence shows every cited re-page came from a restart, not the in-lifetime prune. Both rows were past 2x blockedTimeoutMs at each re-page, and a dep-waiting row past 2x qualifies on every pass, so only a lost memo explains them. 1a8f1d0e's 05:28:45Z page is the first 5-minute sweep after daemon.json startedAt 05:23:45Z. 17 sweeps in #governors paged 2+ standing rows at once (11-01 18:28:34Z: 1a8f1d0e, 48f0b3aa, f4811a72). Option 2 would leave all 15 cited pages in place.
- A dedicated runtime file rejected: a new .moe path needs the root .gitignore, the CLAUDE.md runtime list and the .moe/.gitignore scaffold, plus its own atomic write and corruption handling. The #governors JSONL is already the durable, gitignored record of every page.
- Seeding by task id alone rejected: a later block instance must page again (mutant M4).
- The FIX DIRECTION's resource-less liveKeys was widened to every BLOCKED row with a parseable blockedAt.

- A same-millisecond flake is avoided by the strict '>' and by (c)'s +60s blockedAt.
